text: Log shipping predates Availability Groups, and its simplicity is why it's still in production. It periodically backs up the transaction log on the primary, copies that backup to a secondary, and restores it there — repeated on a schedule.

Log shipping's RPO is directly set by how often the log-backup job runs — the same restore-chain logic from Chapter 13, just automated and pointed at a warm secondary. Every 15 minutes means a 15-minute best-case RPO.

It earns its place in hybrid topologies — an on-prem primary shipping to an Azure VM secondary, or the reverse. It also works on Standard Edition and across a wider range of SQL Server versions than a full AG.

Underneath, it's three SQL Server Agent jobs: a backup job on the primary, a copy job that moves the file, a restore job on the secondary. Bringing a log-shipped secondary online is a deliberate manual step, not automatic.

Higher latency, higher potential data loss, but real and still the right tool for the right hybrid scenario. Next up: actually testing that any of this HA/DR planning works before a real disaster forces the question.
